Except that's what DNS servers do? They literally just take the web address and turn it into the corresponding IP address.
Yes, but addresses in the 192.168/16 block are not routable. The IP address the author uses isn't an internet-facing address and a DNS server would never return it. It's an internal network address.

So the complaint is that they used a sample address instead of posting one of their actual IPs? They just picked two examples. And truth be told most home systems do tend to run www.newyorker.com through 192.168.1.1 it is just that that is the first hop to their own gateway.

Not a sample address, a reserved address. An address that doesn't point to a location on the internet. An address that no DNS server would ever return.
